segments.say: Answered, with the sheet. NVIDIA Nemotron answered from the index and read this sheet, served on a single GPU on a Nebius AI Cloud Serverless endpoint. The boxes are the lettering it relied on.

The Library of Congress holds fifty-five thousand public-domain drawing sets of American buildings. Preservation architects, historians, and the people who maintain these buildings still read them sheet by sheet. None could be asked a question. Until now.

This is Iolani Palace, Honolulu, HABS number H I one: eighty-five pages, twenty-three scanned drawing sheets, fifty-seven photographs, surveyed in 1964 and 1966, several redrawn from the 1903 plans. We say the dates the sheets say.

NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano Omni read every sheet on one L40S on Nebius AI Cloud: title, description, every legible piece of hand lettering with its position, then four quadrants for the small notes. 1,818 entries, read by the model, not typed by us.

Which sheets show the Richards Street elevation. Nemotron answers over the evidence pack the index builds, with the sheets as receipts, verified in code: a page that does not exist is flagged, never shown as fact.

What does HABS sheet 12 reference. Historic sheets cross-reference by lettering, SEE SHEET N. We type those into links, so the answer carries the lettering as its receipt, and the check reports any target missing from the set.

do.text: what wood species is the central stair balustrade

segments.say: And the question every archive tool gets wrong. What wood is the central stair balustrade. The set does not say, so Nemotron answers: not in the set, with the pages it checked. Four outcomes, nothing else.

Open method on open models: MIT on GitHub, every call to NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius, built for Token Factory, read on our own AI Cloud endpoint when the credits ran out. The documents are public domain.
Nemotron on Nebius reads it today, on one GPU. Next, we train the eyes on Token Factory. Nothing invents a sheet.
